- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by > 5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast, targeting 1–2 std dev below recent high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–3 days; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for each lagged day.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33) over 5+ days, model underperforms; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
